mainTopic: The embracing כרובים, the אבן שתיה and where creation began, and the meaning of 'כמצליף'
overview: This amud finishes explaining that the כרובים looked like a man embracing his companion. ריש לקיש then tells how the גוים who entered the היכל took the embracing כרובים out to the market and mocked ישראל, fulfilling the פסוק in איכה. Next the גמרא explains the משנה's name 'אבן שתיה': the world was founded from that stone. It says our משנה follows the view that the world was created from ציון. A ברייתא then brings three views: רבי אליעזר (from the center), רבי יהושע (from the sides), and חכמים (from ציון). רבי יצחק נפחא adds that God cast a stone into the sea. A second ברייתא records רבי אליעזר הגדול, who says heavenly things came from heaven and earthly things from earth, while חכמים say everything came from ציון. Finally the גמרא returns to the משנה's account of the כהן גדול sprinkling the blood and asks what 'כמצליף' means. רב יהודה begins to demonstrate the motion, and his answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The cherubs looked like a man embracing his companion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes explaining the פסוק phrase 'כמער איש ולויות': it describes the כרובים as clinging to each other like a man clinging to his companion.
steps.simpleTranslation: It means like a man who is clinging to his companion.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes explaining an unusual word in a פסוק. It is describing how the carved כרובים in the Temple looked: like two people embracing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'לויות' is read as 'לוויה', a companion who is joined to you. So the carvings showed figures attached to one another. This sets up ריש לקיש's story that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: companion, one who is joined to you (here: a wife)
the winged figures in the Temple

steps.confusionAlert: This line is the end of a discussion that began on the previous amud. It is not a new statement on its own. It completes the explanation of 'כמער איש ולויות'.

phrases.english: Like a man clinging to his companion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the explanation of the פסוק that began on the previous amud.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'לויות' means a companion joined to a man, so the כרובים were shown embracing.

steps.title: The gentiles mock the embracing cherubs
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says that when the גוים entered the היכל, they found the embracing כרובים, brought them out to the market, and mocked the Jews for having such images.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: When the gentiles entered the Sanctuary, they saw כרובים clinging to one another. They took them out to the market and said: 'These Jews, whose blessing is a blessing and whose curse is a curse, should they be busy with such things?'
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש tells a story about the destruction of the בית המקדש. The enemies found the embracing כרובים and used them to mock the Jews in public.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גוים knew that the Jews were respected for their closeness to God, because their blessings and curses came true. They twisted a holy symbol, the love between God and ישראל, into something crude. Their point was: how can such a holy people make images like these?

keyTerms.meaning: a major אמורא of ארץ ישראל
the Sanctuary of the בית המקדש
their blessing is truly a blessing (it comes true)

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
When the gentiles entered the Sanctuary
they saw cherubs clinging to one another,
they took them out to the market and said:
These Jews,
whose blessing is a blessing and whose curse is a curse,
phrases.notes: Meaning they are known to be close to God.

phrases.english: should they be busy with such things?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the description of the embracing כרובים with a story about what happened to them.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The גוים took the embracing כרובים to the market and mocked ישראל over them.

steps.title: The gentiles debased ישראל, as the פסוק in איכה says
steps.stepSummary: Right away the גוים debased ישראל. The story is supported by the פסוק in איכה: 'All who honored her debase her, because they have seen her nakedness.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Immediately they debased them, as it says: 'All who honored her debase her, because they have seen her nakedness.'
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש finishes his story and brings a פסוק to support it. The nations who used to honor ישראל now treated them with contempt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'nakedness' in the פסוק is read as the embracing כרובים, which the nations saw and mocked. People who once respected ישראל ('מכבדיה') now looked down on them. The פסוק fits the story exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: they debased them, treated them as cheap

steps.whatToRemember: Holy symbols that are seen out of context can be twisted by outsiders. The destruction brought a loss of ישראל's honor in the eyes of the nations.

phrases.english: Immediately they debased them, as it is stated:
'All who honored her debase her
because they have seen her nakedness.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes ריש לקיש's story and supports it with a פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: That the nations debased ישראל after seeing the כרובים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: איכה א:ח, 'כל מכבדיה הזילוה כי ראו ערותה'.

steps.title: Why the stone was called שתיה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words 'ושתיה היתה נקראת' and brings a ברייתא: the stone was called שתיה because the world was founded from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And it was called שתיה.' A תנא taught: because from it the world was founded.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a new phrase in the משנה about the stone in the קודש הקדשים. It explains the name 'שתיה' using a teaching of the תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'שתיה' is linked to 'הושתת', meaning 'was founded'. So the stone is named for its role as the starting point of creation. This opens a new topic: where was the world created from?

keyTerms.meaning: the Foundation Stone in the קודש הקדשים
a תנא taught (introduces a teaching from the time of the משנה)

phrases.english: 'And it was called Shetiyah.'
It was taught: because from it the world was founded.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of the כרובים and returns to the משנה's next phrase.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The stone is called שתיה because the world was founded (הושתת) from it.

steps.title: Our משנה follows the view that the world was created from ציון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says that our משנה follows the opinion that the world was created from ציון.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned this according to the one who said that the world was created from ציון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names which opinion the משנה follows. This is a setup line: next it brings the ברייתא that lays out all the opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the world was founded from the stone in the קודש הקדשים, then creation began at ציון. That matches only one side of a debate among the תנאים. The גמרא now has to show us that debate.

keyTerms.meaning: according to the one who said
Zion, the site of the בית המקדש

phrases.english: We learned [our Mishnah] according to the one who said
the world was created from Zion,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a conclusion from the explanation of 'שתיה' about whose opinion the משנה follows.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Our משנה follows the view that creation began from ציון.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: the world was created from its center
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא begins with רבי אליעזר, who says the world was created from its center and grew outward, like clods of earth sticking together.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: רבי אליעזר says: The world was created from its center, as it says: 'When the dust runs into a mass, and the clods cleave together.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts quoting the ברייתא with the different opinions. רבי אליעזר holds that creation started in the middle and spread outward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in איוב describes dust gathering into one solid mass, with more clods sticking on. That is pictured as the world growing from a center point. This is close to the view that it started at ציון.

keyTerms.meaning: as it was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: As it was taught: Rabbi Eliezer says:
The world was created from its center,
as it says: 'When the dust runs into a mass,
and the clods cleave fast together.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the ברייתא that step 5 referred to.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Creation began at the center and spread outward.

steps.title: רבי יהושע: the world was created from the sides
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע says the world was created from the sides, based on a פסוק about snow and rain forming the earth.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע says: The world was created from the sides, as it says: 'For He said to the snow: Become earth, and to the shower of rain, and the showers of His mighty rain.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a second, opposite view. רבי יהושע holds that creation began at the edges and closed in toward the middle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Snow and rain fall everywhere, from all around. So if the earth formed from them, it formed from the sides inward. This disagrees with רבי אליעזר's view that it began from the center.

keyTerms.meaning: a major תנא, often disputing רבי אליעזר

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua says:
The world was created from the sides,
as it says: 'For He said to the snow: Become the earth,
likewise to the shower of rain, and the showers of His mighty rain.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רבי אליעזר within the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Creation began at the edges, not the center.

steps.title: רבי יצחק נפחא: a stone cast into the sea
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק נפחא, an אמורא, adds that הקדוש ברוך הוא threw a stone into the sea and the world was founded from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק נפחא said: הקדוש ברוך הוא threw a stone into the sea, and from it the world was founded, as it says: 'Upon what were its foundations sunk, or who cast its cornerstone?'
steps.whatsHappening: In the middle of the ברייתא, the גמרא adds a view from a later אמורא. He gives another picture of how creation began: from one stone thrown into the waters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק uses the word 'ירה' (cast) for the cornerstone, and 'הטבעו' (sunk) for the foundations, as if they sank into water. So רבי יצחק reads it as a stone thrown into the sea, from which the land spread out. His word 'נשתת' echoes the name 'שתיה'.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי יצחק נפחא is not part of the ברייתא. He is a later אמורא whose view is inserted between רבי יהושע and חכמים. The ברייתא continues afterward with 'וחכמים אומרים'.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha said:

phrases.aramaic: אֶבֶן יָרָה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בַּיָּם,
phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, cast a stone into the sea,
from which the world was founded,
as it says: 'Upon what were its foundations sunk,
or who cast its cornerstone?'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: An אמורא's view inserted into the list of opinions from the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The world was founded from a stone that God cast into the sea.

steps.title: חכמים: the world was created from ציון
steps.stepSummary: חכמים say the world was created from ציון, citing the opening of תהלים נ, where God calls the earth into being.
steps.simpleTranslation: חכמים say: It was created from ציון, as it says: 'A Psalm of אסף. God, the Lord God [has spoken and called the earth].'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the view of חכמים, which is the view our משנה follows (step 5). They hold that creation began at ציון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes God calling forth the whole earth, 'from the rising of the sun to its setting'. Read together with the next פסוק (step 10), that call came out of ציון. This is the source the גמרא promised in step 5.

phrases.english: And the Sages say: It was created from Zion,
as it says: 'A Psalm of Asaph. God, the Lord God...'
phrases.notes: תהלים נ:א; the פסוק continues 'has spoken and called the earth'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ברייתא and gives the view that step 5 said our משנה follows.

steps.title: From ציון the beauty of the world was perfected
steps.stepSummary: חכמים add a second פסוק, 'מציון מכלל יופי', and read it as: from ציון the world's beauty was completed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it also says: 'Out of ציון, the perfection of beauty.' This means from it the beauty of the world was completed.
steps.whatsHappening: חכמים bring a second פסוק to make their proof clear. It ties the creation of the world directly to ציון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק alone only says God called the earth. The next פסוק says 'from ציון', which tells us where the call came from. 'מכלל יופי' is read as 'מוכלל יפיו של עולם': the world's beauty was completed from ציון, so creation started there, just as our משנה's 'אבן שתיה' implies.

keyTerms.meaning: and it also says (introduces a second proof פסוק)

steps.whatToRemember: Our משנה's name 'אבן שתיה' follows חכמים, who hold that creation began at ציון. Other views say from the center (רבי אליעזר), from the sides (רבי יהושע), or from a stone cast into the sea (רבי יצחק נפחא).
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the place of the קודש הקדשים is seen as the starting point and spiritual center of the whole world.

phrases.english: And it says: 'Out of Zion, the perfection of beauty' —
from it the beauty of the world was perfected.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second פסוק to complete חכמים' proof.
steps.raayaObject: That the world was created from ציון, so our משנה follows חכמים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: תהלים נ:ב, 'מציון מכלל יופי', read as 'from it the world's beauty was perfected'.

steps.title: Heavenly things came from heaven, earthly things came from earth
steps.stepSummary: In a new ברייתא, רבי אליעזר הגדול reads בראשית ב:ד to mean that everything in the heavens was created from the heavens, and everything on earth was created from the earth.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי אליעזר הגדול says: 'These are the generations of the heaven and the earth when they were created, on the day that ה׳ אלהים made earth and heaven.' 'The generations of heaven' means they were created from heaven. 'The generations of the earth' means they were created from earth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא. In it, רבי אליעזר הגדול says each part of creation came from its own place: heavenly things from heaven, earthly things from earth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word תולדות ('offspring') suggests that something grew out of a source. רבי אליעזר הגדול reads 'offspring of the heavens' as things born from the heavens, and 'offspring of the earth' as things born from the earth. This means there were two separate starting points, not one.

keyTerms.meaning: רבי אליעזר the Great, a תנא
Generations / offspring, things that come out of a source

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Eliezer the Great says:
"These are the generations of the heaven and the earth when they were created,

phrases.aramaic: בְּיוֹם עֲשׂוֹת ה׳ אֱלֹהִים אֶרֶץ וְשָׁמָיִם״,
phrases.english: on the day that the Lord God made earth and heaven"
"Generations of heaven": they were created from heaven,
"generations of the earth": they were created from earth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a second ברייתא about where creation began. It is separate from the earlier ברייתא about the center and the sides.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Heavenly things were created from the heavens, and earthly things were created from the earth.

steps.title: חכמים say both heaven and earth came from ציון
steps.stepSummary: חכמים disagree with רבי אליעזר הגדול. They say both the heavenly things and the earthly things were created from ציון, and they cite תהלים נ:א.
steps.simpleTranslation: And חכמים say: both these and those were created from ציון, as it says: 'A Psalm of אסף. God, the Lord God has spoken and called the earth, from the rising of the sun to its setting.'
steps.whatsHappening: חכמים answer רבי אליעזר הגדול. They say there was only one source for all of creation, and that source was ציון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר הגדול had two starting points. חכמים have one: ציון. The פסוק in תהלים describes God calling out to the whole earth, and the next פסוק says this came from ציון. So the whole world spread out from that one place.

keyTerms.meaning: These and those, meaning both the heavenly and the earthly things
From ציון, the site of the בית המקדש
As it is said (introduces a פסוק as proof)

steps.confusionAlert: Yes, you saw this statement of חכמים in the earlier ברייתא as well. The גמרא is quoting a second ברייתא, where the same view of חכמים now answers a different opponent: רבי אליעזר הגדול.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:
both these and those were created from Zion,
as it is stated: "A Psalm of Asaph.

phrases.aramaic: אֵל אֱלֹהִים ה׳ דִּבֶּר וַיִּקְרָא אָרֶץ
phrases.english: God, the Lord God has spoken and called the earth,
from the rising of the sun to its place of setting."

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: אֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ מִצִּיּוֹן נִבְרְאוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רבי אליעזר הגדול in the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All of creation, both heavenly and earthly, came from ציון.

steps.title: A second פסוק: the world's beauty was completed from ציון
steps.stepSummary: חכמים add תהלים נ:ב, 'מציון מכלל יופי'. They read it as saying that the beauty of the whole world was completed from ציון.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it says: 'Out of ציון, the perfection of beauty, God has shined forth.' This means that from ציון, the beauty of the world was completed.
steps.whatsHappening: חכמים bring a second פסוק. It mentions ציון by name and so supports their view directly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק spoke about the whole earth, but it did not name ציון. This פסוק names ציון. חכמים read מכלל ('perfection') as מוכלל ('completed'), so the world's whole beauty, both heaven and earth, was completed from ציון.

keyTerms.meaning: And it says (introduces an additional proof-פסוק)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר הגדול says heavenly things came from heaven and earthly things came from earth. חכמים say everything came from ציון. That is why ציון, the place of the בית המקדש and the אבן שתיה, is called the foundation of the world.

phrases.english: And it says: "Out of Zion, the perfection of beauty,
God has shined forth"
from it the beauty of the world was perfected.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, clearer proof for the view of חכמים in step 12.
steps.raayaObject: The claim of חכמים that both heaven and earth were created from ציון
steps.raayaSupportSource: תהלים נ:ב, 'מציון מכלל יופי אלהים הופיע', read as 'from ציון the world's beauty was completed'

steps.title: Back to the משנה: taking the blood from the one stirring it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה. It quotes the line where the כהן גדול takes the bull's blood from the person who was stirring it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'He took the blood from the one who was stirring it, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: The creation discussion is over, and the גמרא goes back to the משנה. This line is a setup: the גמרא quotes the משנה so that it can ask about a word in it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום הכפורים, someone kept stirring the blood of the פר so it would not clot before the כהן גדול was ready. The כהן גדול then took the blood, went into the קודש הקדשים, and sprinkled it. The וכו׳ points to the rest of the משנה, including the word כמצליף, which the גמרא will now explain.

keyTerms.meaning: The blood (here, of the כהן גדול's bull)
Stirs, keeping blood moving so it does not clot
Etc., meaning the quote continues in the משנה

phrases.english: He took the blood
from the one who was stirring it, etc.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָטַל אֶת הַדָּם מִמִּי שֶׁמְּמָרֵס בּוֹ וְכוּ׳
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the creation discussion and returns to the משנה's account of the עבודה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהן גדול takes the bull's blood from the person stirring it and goes in to sprinkle it, as the משנה describes.

steps.title: What does 'like one who whips' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the משנה means by saying the כהן גדול sprinkled כמצליף, 'like one who whips'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple question about what a word means. It wants to know what hand motion the כהן גדול used to sprinkle the blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not an attack on the משנה. It is a request for clarity. The word כמצליף compares the sprinkling to whipping, and the גמרא wants to know exactly what that motion looks like.

keyTerms.meaning: Like one who whips; describes the sprinkling motion

phrases.english: What is: Like one who whips?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a word from the משנה quoted in step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact hand motion meant by כמצליף when sprinkling the blood

steps.title: רב יהודה shows the motion with his hand
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה answers by acting out the motion. The description of what he showed continues in the next part of the גמרא.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה starts to answer the question by showing the motion with his hand instead of only explaining it in words. The sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some actions are easier to show than to describe. The word מחוי tells us that רב יהודה acted out the motion. The גמרא will next describe what he showed.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda demonstrated
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to the question in step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב יהודה shows the motion physically. The details follow on the next amud.
